title: Quote-Batched Payment Protocol for Reducing First-Proposal Bias in Agentic Marketplaces

contributions.purpose: Reduce first-proposal bias, the tendency of LLM customer agents to disproportionately select the first proposal they receive in agentic marketplaces.
contributions.mechanism: QuoteBatch, an environment-level mechanism-design protocol combining a hard-gate that blocks payment until a minimum number of proposals arrive with anti-anchoring prompt instructions, deployable with any LLM without retraining.
contributions.evaluation: Method-level; quantitative effect reported in C2.
contributions.domain: LLM agents in economic marketplaces (Magentic Marketplace)
contributions.source_quote: We introduce QuoteBatch, a mechanism design protocol that combines hard-gate payment blocking with anti-anchoring instructions to reduce first-proposal bias in agentic marketplaces.

contributions.purpose: Quantify QuoteBatch's effectiveness at reducing first-proposal bias on a strong LLM.
contributions.mechanism: Apply QuoteBatch to a Claude customer agent in the Magentic Marketplace and measure first-proposal rate and task completion.
contributions.evaluation: Achieves a 93.3 percentage-point reduction in first-proposal bias on Claude claude-sonnet-4-5 (from 100% to 6.7%, p<0.001) while maintaining 100% task completion.
contributions.source_quote: We demonstrate that QuoteBatch achieves a 93.3 percentage point reduction in first-proposal bias on Claude claude-sonnet-4-5 (from 100% to 6.7%, p<0.001) while maintaining 100% task completion.

contributions.purpose: Characterize how mechanism-design effectiveness varies across different LLMs.
contributions.mechanism: Apply the same QuoteBatch intervention to a Gemini agent and compare bias reduction.
contributions.evaluation: Substantial model heterogeneity: the same intervention yields only a 10 percentage-point reduction on Gemini gemini-2.5-flash (not statistically significant), highlighting that bias mitigation may need to be model-specific.
contributions.source_quote: We reveal substantial model heterogeneity: the same intervention yields only a 10 percentage point reduction on Gemini gemini-2.5-flash, highlighting that bias mitigation strategies may need to be model-specific.

contributions.purpose: Determine which component of QuoteBatch drives the bias reduction.
contributions.mechanism: Ablation studies isolating the anti-anchoring prompt from the hard-gate payment blocker on Claude.
contributions.evaluation: The anti-anchoring prompt is identified as the critical component, improving first-proposal rate from 60% to 6.7% on Claude.
contributions.source_quote: Through ablation studies, we identify the anti-anchoring prompt as the critical component for bias reduction on Claude, improving first-proposal rate from 60% to 6.7%.

self_declared_provenance.quote: Valencia-Clavijo (2025) provide behavioral and attributional evidence of anchoring bias in LLMs... Our work extends this literature by examining first-proposal bias in economic decision-making and proposing mechanism design interventions to mitigate it.

Most relevant to our work, Bansal et al. (2025) present Magentic Marketplace, an open-source environment for studying agentic markets where customer agents interact with contractor agents to complete tasks. Our work builds directly on this platform to study first-proposal bias and evaluate mechanism design interventions.
Unlike prior work that primarily evaluates LLM economic behavior, our work proposes and evaluates mechanism design interventions to modify agent behavior without model retraining.

notes: Partial-negative / heterogeneity result flagged by the paper: QuoteBatch works strongly on Claude (93.3pp) but yields only a 10pp reduction on Gemini 2.5-flash (explicitly not statistically significant), indicating the intervention does not generalize across models.
